comments.body:
Plan review v1 returned BLOCK on criterion E4 (correctly): the description specified the retire target as a `rebar-mcp-<sha>` IMAGE, but no such image exists. Verified against the shipped script:

- image tag = `"$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"` = `compose-mcp:<40-char-sha>` (autodeploy.sh:763 tags it, :406 runs it; MCP_IMAGE defaults to `compose-mcp` at :146)
- container name = `"${MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX}-${TARGET:0:12}-${mcp_newport}"` = `rebar-mcp-<sha12>-<port>` (:783, prefix at :147)

So `rebar-mcp-<sha>` names a CONTAINER, not an image. Following AC1 literally would have produced a `docker rmi rebar-mcp-<sha>` that silently no-ops, leaving the exact leak this ticket exists to fix. Description corrected.

Because the container name carries only a truncated sha plus the port, it must not be string-manipulated back into an image tag; the retire path reads the exact reference from `docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' <container>` BEFORE `docker rm` (it is unreadable afterwards).

Also folded in the three advisories: counter persistence + fail-safe (E2/T5b), the streak threshold as a named `PRESSURE_STREAK_ALARM` constant rather than a prose literal (T5e), and an explicit out-of-scope note for the pre-existing orphaned-tag backlog (G6).

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The MCP endpoint became unreachable on 2026-08-28. The container was healthy (local probe:
`200` in 1.8ms) but external requests timed out, because nginx was buffering to
`/var/lib/nginx/tmp/` on a root disk at **92% (2.6G free)**. Reclaiming docker garbage took it
to **57%** and the endpoint recovered immediately.

## Why the automatic reclaim did not self-heal it

`prune_docker_caches()` (`autodeploy.sh:276-284`) runs a capped
`docker builder prune -f --keep-storage "$BUILD_CACHE_KEEP"` plus `docker image prune -f`:

1. `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP` defaults to `5GB` (`:124`) and the cache measured **5.254GB** — the
   prune retained it BY DESIGN.
2. `docker image prune -f` without `-a` removes only DANGLING images (`:272` states the
   intent). Blue-green tags every build with an immutable per-release tag, so the box held
   **44 images / 11.09GB, 10.08GB reclaimable**. Tagged-image accumulation is the dominant
   leak and nothing is permitted to remove it.

So the gate ran on schedule, logged `"disk pressure reclaim complete"`, freed ~nothing, then
throttled for 600s and repeated that misleading success. `observability.sh:330-335` claims its
marker lets an incident sweep *"distinguish 'the reclaim gate never ran' from 'it ran and
reclaimed nothing'"* without host access. It cannot: it counts INVOCATIONS, not bytes freed.

### The actual tag scheme (corrected 2026-08-28)

An earlier revision called the per-release image `rebar-mcp-<sha>`. Wrong:

* **Image tag** — `"$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"` = `compose-mcp:<40-char-sha>`, tagged at
  `autodeploy.sh:763`, consumed by `mcp_run_new` at `:406`. `MCP_IMAGE` defaults to
  `compose-mcp` (`:146`), so ALL releases share one image NAME and differ only in the TAG.
* **Container name** — `"${MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX}-${TARGET:0:12}-${mcp_newport}"` (`:783`) =
  `rebar-mcp-<sha12>-<port>` (`:147`). So `rebar-mcp-<sha>` names a CONTAINER, never an image.
* **No `compose-mcp:prev` (or explicit `:latest`) is ever created.** `:prev` is a `$BOT_IMAGE`
  scheme only (`:676`/`:679`/`:689`). The mcp target's rollback is the blue-green mechanism
  itself: on an unhealthy/storeless new container or a failed flip it `docker rm -f`s the NEW
  container and leaves the OLD one serving the unchanged upstream (`:801`, `:827`, `:837`).

Because the container name carries only a TRUNCATED sha plus the port, it must NOT be
string-manipulated back into an image tag. The mapping comes from ASKING DOCKER:
`docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' <container>` returns the exact `compose-mcp:<sha>`
reference that container was started from. That is the identifier the retire path removes.

Alerting was not the gap: `rebar-root-disk-pressure` (85%) **did fire** and sat in ALARM ~11
hours, flapping as the reclaim freed a little and the disk refilled. A threshold alarm cannot
say "reclaim is running and achieving nothing" — the actionable condition.

## Scope (operator-directed, 2026-08-28)

1. **Retire the per-release `compose-mcp:<sha>` image once its container is fully drained and
   reaped.** The blue-green retire path (`mcp_retire_sweep`) already reaps exited containers
   with `docker rm`; removing that container's image belongs there — AFTER the reap succeeds,
   never while serving. The image reference is read with
   `docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' <container>` BEFORE the `docker rm` (it is
   unreadable afterwards). Two references are retained: the bare `$MCP_IMAGE` build tag (the
   `docker compose build mcp` output `:763` re-tags each deploy) and the LIVE backend's image.
   Removal uses `docker image rm` WITHOUT `-f`, so the daemon itself refuses while any
   container still references the image — an independent second guard.
2. **Log root-disk free space before and after every reclaim**, plus the delta, so effect is
   observable rather than inferred.
3. **Emit a loud, distinct marker when pressure persists across 3 or more reclaim cycles** —
   the "reclaim is ineffective" signal that no existing alarm expresses.

### The streak state machine — one rule per tick outcome

`reclaim_under_pressure` has THREE outcomes, and the counter is defined on each:

1. **Below threshold** — the early return at `:302`. The RESET lives HERE, *before* that
   return, not next to the increment: a recovered tick never reaches the post-reclaim code, so
   a reset placed there would be unreachable and the counter would never clear.
2. **Pressured but THROTTLED** (`:307-310`, within `PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL`) — UNCHANGED.
   It counts reclaim CYCLES, not ticks: a throttled tick ran no reclaim, so it is evidence
   neither for nor against effectiveness. This keeps the marker honest — at a ~2-min tick and
   a 600s throttle, counting ticks would reach 3 inside ONE throttle window, firing while only
   a single reclaim had run.
3. **Reclaim RAN** — re-read `root_disk_pct()` AFTER the prune. Still `>= DISK_PRESSURE_PCT`:
   increment. Below it: reset to `0` (the reclaim worked).

### Persistence and configurability

The gate runs as a SEPARATE process per ~2-min tick, so the counter is persisted on disk,
mirroring `PRESSURE_PRUNE_TS_FILE` (`autodeploy.sh:133`): a file under `$STATE_DIR` named by an
overridable `PRESSURE_STREAK_FILE`, written write-tmp-then-`mv` so a torn write is never
observed. It **fails safe toward silence** — absent, unreadable, or non-numeric reads as `0`,
so a lost counter delays the marker rather than emitting a false one. The threshold is a named
overridable constant `PRESSURE_STREAK_ALARM` (default `3`), consistent with the existing
`DISK_PRESSURE_PCT` / `PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL` tunables — not a hardcoded literal.

### Out of scope: the pre-existing tag backlog

The reclaim is retire-path-only. Tags orphaned earlier — including any reaped in the crash
window between `docker rm` and the image removal — have no future reap event and are ACCEPTED
as residue: the backlog was already cleared manually (44 images -> 4), so steady state is
bounded. An unconditional `docker image prune -a` is NOT adopted — it cannot distinguish the
live release from garbage. Draining residue stays a manual operator action.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a blue-green container is reaped, the `compose-mcp:<sha>` image it was running is
      removed, while the live backend's image and the bare `$MCP_IMAGE` build tag are retained
      (checked by a test that reaps a fake container and asserts exactly which image references
      survive).
- [ ] A serving container's image is NEVER removed — the retire path removes an image only
      after the `docker rm` for that container has succeeded (checked by a test that seeds a
      RUNNING container and asserts no image removal is issued for it).
- [ ] `prune_docker_caches` logs root-disk free space BEFORE and AFTER, and the delta, on every
      invocation (checked by asserting both values and the delta appear in the emitted log line).
- [ ] When a reclaim completes and the disk is STILL at or above `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT`, the
      persisted streak counter increments; a below-threshold tick resets it to zero even though
      it takes the early return; a throttled pressured tick leaves it unchanged (checked by
      driving the counter across a pressure / throttle / relief sequence).
- [ ] At `PRESSURE_STREAK_ALARM` (default 3) or more consecutive ineffective cycles, a distinct
      marker is emitted (not the existing `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE`, which counts invocations)
      and `observability.sh` publishes it as its own delta metric, so it is alarmable without
      host access.
- [ ] The new marker fires only on PERSISTENCE: a single pressured cycle that then recovers does
      NOT emit it (checked by a negative-control test — this is the discriminator, since an
      alarm that fires on any pressure is the flapping alarm we already have).

## Evidence

Disk 92%->57%; images 44->4 (11.09GB->2.779GB); build cache 5.254GB->0; endpoint went from four
12s timeouts to six 401s at ~250ms.
